examples.question_text: When it is $8{:}20\text{ am}$ in Alice Springs ($\text{UTC}+9.5$), what is the local time in Fremantle ($\text{UTC}+8$)?
examples.solution_text:
Fremantle is behind Alice Springs.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=9.5-8\\&=1.5\text{ h}\\&=1\text{ h }30\text{ min}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Time in Fremantle}&=08{:}20-1\text{ h }30\text{ min}\\&=06{:}50\end{aligned}$
It is $6{:}50\text{ am}$ in Fremantle.

examples.question_text:
Find the local day and time in each case.
(a) It is $9{:}15\text{ am}$ on Wednesday in Sydney ($\text{UTC}+10$). What time is it in San Francisco ($\text{UTC}-8$)?
(b) It is $8{:}40\text{ pm}$ on Monday in Anchorage ($\text{UTC}-9$). What time is it in Tokyo ($\text{UTC}+9$)?
examples.solution_text:
(a) San Francisco is $10-(-8)=18\text{ h}$ behind Sydney. Subtracting $18\text{ h}$ crosses midnight, so use the previous day.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Time in San Francisco}&=(24\text{ h}+9\text{ h }15\text{ min})-18\text{ h}\\&=15\text{ h }15\text{ min}\end{aligned}$
It is $3{:}15\text{ pm}$ on Tuesday.

(b) Tokyo is $9-(-9)=18\text{ h}$ ahead of Anchorage.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Time in Tokyo}&=20{:}40+18\text{ h}\\&=38{:}40\\&=14{:}40\text{ on the next day}\end{aligned}$
It is $2{:}40\text{ pm}$ on Tuesday.

examples.question_text:
Sydney uses standard time ($\text{UTC}+10$). San Francisco moves its clocks forward $1\text{ h}$ from standard time ($\text{UTC}-8$) for daylight saving.
A flight leaves Sydney at $8{:}45\text{ pm}$ on Wednesday and takes $13\text{ h }35\text{ min}$. Find the local arrival day and time in San Francisco.
examples.solution_text:
San Francisco's daylight-saving offset is $-8+1=-7$. It is $10-(-7)=17\text{ h}$ behind Sydney.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Departure in San Francisco}&=20{:}45-17\text{ h}\\&=03{:}45\text{ on Wednesday}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Arrival in San Francisco}&=03{:}45+13\text{ h }35\text{ min}\\&=17{:}20\text{ on Wednesday}\end{aligned}$
The flight arrives at $5{:}20\text{ pm}$ on Wednesday.

examples.question_text:
Brisbane ($\text{UTC}+10$) is $4.5\text{ h}$ ahead of New Delhi ($\text{UTC}+5.5$).
A passenger leaves New Delhi at $12{:}20\text{ pm}$ on Monday, spends $2\text{ h }30\text{ min}$ at a stopover, and arrives in Brisbane at $8{:}10\text{ am}$ on Tuesday. Calculate the total flying time.
examples.solution_text:
Express departure and arrival in Brisbane time.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Departure in Brisbane}&=12{:}20+4\text{ h }30\text{ min}\\&=16{:}50\text{ on Monday}\end{aligned}$
From $16{:}50$ to midnight is $7\text{ h }10\text{ min}$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Elapsed time}&=7\text{ h }10\text{ min}+8\text{ h }10\text{ min}\\&=15\text{ h }20\text{ min}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Flying time}&=15\text{ h }20\text{ min}-2\text{ h }30\text{ min}\\&=12\text{ h }50\text{ min}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
A flight leaves point $A(10^{\circ}\text{N},45^{\circ}\text{W})$ at $9{:}30\text{ am}$ local solar time on Tuesday for point $B(20^{\circ}\text{N},75^{\circ}\text{E})$. The flight takes $6\text{ h }30\text{ min}$.
Using $15^{\circ}=1\text{ h}$, find the local solar arrival day and time at $B$.
examples.solution_text:
The longitudes are on opposite sides of the prime meridian. Point $B$ is further east, so it is ahead.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=45^{\circ}+75^{\circ}\\&=120^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=120\div15\\&=8\text{ h}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Departure time at }B&=09{:}30+8\text{ h}\\&=17{:}30\text{ on Tuesday}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Arrival time at }B&=17{:}30+6\text{ h }30\text{ min}\\&=24{:}00\\&=00{:}00\text{ on Wednesday}\end{aligned}$
The flight arrives at midnight at the start of Wednesday, local solar time.

examples.question_text:
An online presentation starts at $7{:}30\text{ pm}$ on Thursday at a location with longitude $20^{\circ}\text{E}$ and lasts $1\text{ h }45\text{ min}$.
Find the local solar day and time when it finishes at a location with longitude $140^{\circ}\text{E}$. Use $15^{\circ}=1\text{ h}$ and ignore daylight saving.
examples.solution_text:
The second location is further east, so it is ahead.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=140^{\circ}-20^{\circ}\\&=120^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=120\div15\\&=8\text{ h}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Presentation start}&=19{:}30+8\text{ h}\\&=27{:}30\\&=03{:}30\text{ on Friday}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Presentation finish}&=03{:}30+1\text{ h }45\text{ min}\\&=05{:}15\text{ on Friday}\end{aligned}$
It finishes at $5{:}15\text{ am}$ on Friday, local solar time.
